# E8 — restructuring depth: may the model rewrite again what a kept rewrite leaves or exposes?

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** done

## The question

After the agent keeps a rewrite it profiles the program again and may find new regions. At depth 0 — every experiment so far — such a region gets DiscoPoP's pragma at most, never a second rewrite; at depth 1 the model may be asked about it once more. Does a second level parallelize regions the first level's rewrites exposed, and what does it cost in calls, profiles and the speed of the result? (RQ8, H8; C1, C3)

## Result in one paragraph

Done (15 Oct): H8 not established — on the depth set, depth 1 race-free FASTER in 8 of 15 trials and depth 0 in 9 of 15 (CMH one-sided p 0.90, exact 0.92; family bound 1; one loop informative); a refutation condition of 14 Sep is met on its own terms (depth 1 added no correct speed-up on the depth set); the sequential cost rose there on `s2251` and `s257` and fell on `s221`, and rose on the 18 loops. On the 18 loops depth 1 34 of 54 and depth 2 28 of 54 against E3's depth 0 75 of 90, with three wrong programs (BROKEN) where depth 0 shipped none — each the last level's rewrite, copying an array where the copy misses the change `dummy()` makes between repetitions, at positions the program's printed digest does not read. In 54 of the 138 depth trials Settle found the finished program slower than the original and undid it (none at depth 0). Before: Running (14 Oct, the author's "ok" at 20:17 UTC): the four counted runs launched on the agent with Fix 106 and Fix 108 — the depth set × depth 0, 1 and 2 × 5 and the 18 loops × depth 1 and 2 × 3, one run per 12-core group; then the race check and the read-out as pre-registered. Before: Held (14 Oct, 19:54 UTC): Fix 108 is in and checked without a model; the third smoke shipped a chain of two rewrites FASTER (2.38×) and ran the new check at the timing size where it should, but its criterion as written flagged the two-round trial (a definition of mine that did not foresee Settle removing a slower program); launching the 153 trials now, or a fourth smoke first, is the author's. Before: Repair approved (14 Oct, the author's "ok" at 18:12 UTC): Fix 108 — with a deeper level to come, the program with DiscoPoP's pragmas is still run once at the timing size and a crash sends the rewrite back as at depth 0; a failure of the program before a rewrite is never charged to it — checked without a model, then a third smoke, then the 153 trials as registered. Before: Held again (14 Oct, 15:21 UTC): Fix 106 is in and checked without a model; the second smoke showed a deeper chain reaching the finished program once, and a second defect of depth as built — with a deeper level to come a rewrite that crashes at the timing size is kept untested and every later attempt is blamed for that crash (candidate Fix 108); its repair, or the launch as built, is the author's. Before: Repair approved (14 Oct, the author's "ok" at 13:23 UTC): Fix 106 — Settle keeps a rewrite that a later kept rewrite was built on — checked without a model, then a second smoke on the repaired agent, then the 153 trials as registered. Before: Held (14 Oct, 08:32 UTC): the smoke passed its criterion and showed that the agent's last check (Settle) throws away every chain of rewrites in which a later one reshapes what an earlier one exposed — both smoke trials no-change after kept rewrites at 1.76× and 2.69×; the four counted runs are not launched; a repair of the check, or the runs on the agent as built, is the author's. Before: Running (14 Oct, the author's "ok" at 07:45 UTC): pre-registered before any trial — a smoke of the two deeper settings, then 45 trials on the depth set (s2251, s221, s257 × depth 0, 1 and 2 × 5) and 108 on the 18 loops (depth 1 and 2 × 3; depth 0 is E3's cells), the agent as built, DiscoPoP writing the pragma; one test, of H8 on the depth set (no new member of the family). Before: Open again (13 Oct, the author: "run both"), the launch held until a benchmark that can show depth is built (his rule of 26 Sep). Built and checked without a model (14 Oct): of six TSVC candidates in the clean form three pass the inclusion rule — s2251, s221, s257, each a chain of two dependent rewrites; s233 is parallel for DiscoPoP alone; s123's first step and no step of s2111 is confirmed by DiscoPoP (candidate B27: a dependence only the outer loop carries is held against the inner loop). The set and its cost go to the author before any model call. The read-out of the archive stands: at depth 0 a deeper level would re-ask in 80 of 80 trials and find a new loop in 4.

$52.08 for E3's 90 trials, $47.03 and $51.09 for the 54 at depth 1 and 2). **The depth set — the form each shipped program reached, read program by program against the references (`reference_solutions/tsvc_c5/`):** `s2251` — at every depth the changed programs have both loops parallel (the final form) except one depth-0 program with one of the two (parallel-not-faster): the model did both steps in one rewrite at depth 0 in 4 of 5 trials, as said before the run ("`default_v5` wins where the model does both steps in one rewrite"); two depth-2 programs carry a copy of `b` per repetition (1.29×, 1.49×). `s257` — at depth 0 all five stop at step 1 (the inner loop parallel per row, 3.1–4.6× at 6 threads); the final form (the recurrence split out, the outer loop parallel, 6.5–7.6×) is reached in 1 of 5 trials at depth 1 and 2 of 5 at depth 2, each by the last level's rewrite (D40 6.72×, 4.88×, 5.96×) — the one place in E8 where a deeper level made parallel what depth 0 did not; the test cannot show it, `s257` being FASTER in every arm (said before the run); two depth-1 programs added a parallel loop over the rows without the split (4.1×, 4.9×). `s221` — no arm faster in any of its 15 trials: at depth 0 D40 sent 4–8 rewrites per trial back as not faster, at depth 1 and 2 every chain was undone by Settle (below), so the open question of its count (the author's) changes no number. **The 18 loops (no test):** per loop in `e8_readout.md`; the FASTER programs are no faster than depth 0's — median speed-up 2.16, 2.17 and 2.36 at 6 threads, 2.54, 2.59 and 2.54 at 12 (`by_hand/speed_by_depth.txt`; depth 1 or 2 more than 10 % above depth 0 on six loops, below on others, with 1–3 FASTER trials a cell). **The three properties of depth as built, measured.** (1) *No speed question at a level a deeper one follows:* in 54 of the 138 depth trials (depth 1: 21, depth 2: 33; the depth set 15, the 18 loops 39) Settle's check of the finished program found it slower than the original — 111 repairs, every one "slower than the original" — dropped its pragmas one by one and then each rewrite as an orphan; all 54 ended no-change, and they are every no-change at depth; at depth 0 not one such repair, in E8's 15 trials or E3's 90. (2) *A second rewrite timed with the first one's gain:* 76 of the 77 FASTER depth trials kept a rewrite at a deeper level (depth 1: 41 of 42, depth 2: 35 of 35), each judged against a program whose earlier rewrites' pragmas were still deferred; outside `s257`'s three, their programs are no faster than depth 0's — the deeper level re-shaped what depth 0 makes parallel and was credited with it. (3) *Only rewrites DiscoPoP confirms in part can be chained* (13 Oct): not tested by trials — the strict loops `s123` and `s2111` were not run (the author); every chain of the depth set is of the kind it allows. **The three wrong programs, read by hand** (`by_hand/README.md`): `e8v5_r_2` `tsvc_c2/s121` `depth1_v5` rep2, `e8v5_r_2` `tsvc_c2/s281` `depth1_v5` rep1, `e8v5_r_1` `tsvc_c2/s127` `depth2_v5` rep3. In each the wrong rewrite is the LAST level's — `s121`'s and `s127`'s of the repetition loop, `s281`'s of the function — judged `ok` by D40 (3.27×, 2.20×, 1.99×); the rewrites kept before it are correct (the row below said each kept a rewrite with the speed question deferred: true, and not the cause). Each copies an array to break a dependence and takes the copy where it misses the change `dummy()` makes to that array between two repetitions (`s121` copies `a` for the next repetition before `dummy()`, `s281` refreshes its copy of `a` before `dummy()`, `s127` computes with a copy of `c` taken before the `dummy()` call that now precedes the computation), so it reads, at the positions `dummy()` changes, values one repetition old. Why the agent passed them: its gate compares the program's printed output byte for byte at the check size on two inputs (noise floor 0), and that output is the harness's digest — sums over both ends, the middle 32 and every `LEN_1D / 2000`-th value (every 16th at SMALL; `pb_emit_array`, packaging v6); the race check reads the same digest; only the harness's verification also builds with `-DPB_FULL_DUMP`, which prints every value. Replayed on the Mac (sequential builds at SMALL, both inputs): digests byte-identical, 46, 68 and 1 of 160,001 values different (largest relative difference 0.0052, 0.0039, 0.062), none on a position the digest reads (`s121`'s and `s127`'s all at an index ≡ 14 mod 16, `s281`'s never ≡ 0). What the author was told twice before this reading (03:32 UTC and after the re-runs started), that the checksums agree, is so — and is the finding: they do not see these values. None of E3's 220 agent trials (110 in each setup) shipped a wrong program. **Fix 106, candidate Fix 107, Fix 108 (counted as registered):** Fix 106 kept a rewrite (`[keep]`) in 65 of 153 trials (133 rewrites). Fix 107's signature in 0 of 153; the 54 trials listed with its pattern after a repair, to be read by hand, are exactly the 54 of property (1): in each the finished program kept no pragma, so no orphan drop could have missed one (`by_hand/fix107_by_hand.txt`) — no case of Fix 107 in E8.
